name: Azelaic acid
lead: Azelaic acid is a naturally occurring dicarboxylic acid used topically for acne, rosacea and post-inflammatory or melasma-type hyperpigmentation. Prescription strengths of 15 to 20 percent exist, and lower-strength cosmetic versions are sold over the counter in many markets.
Its appeal is breadth: a single ingredient that addresses bumps, redness and dark marks, and it is generally acceptable in people who cannot tolerate retinoids.

paras: Azelaic acid has antibacterial effects against acne-associated bacteria, normalizes follicular keratinization, suppresses inflammatory pathways and reactive oxygen species, and competitively inhibits tyrosinase in overactive melanocytes, which explains its use in hyperpigmentation.

Stinging, itching and dryness are the most common effects and usually fade with continued use. Systemic absorption is low and it is widely considered compatible with pregnancy, though individual advice should come from a clinician. Results take weeks to months.
